title: Codex asks with request_user_input, by name, and says so when it cannot
name: Codex asks with request_user_input, by
description: Reported: working in Codex (ChatGPT), the agent never uses the built-in question tool — decisions, approvals and merges are asked in prose or not at all. Cause on our side: `plugins/hosts/codex.json` slot `ask` says only "this host's own question tool" and never names it, while `claude.json` names AskUserQuestion. Name Codex's tool (`request_user_input`) in the `ask` slot, and in the same sentence say what to do when the tool is not offered in the current mode: ask in the conversation exactly as `plugins/hosts/opencode.json` does (options in full, wait for a reply that names one). First check against the installed `codex` version which modes expose `request_user_input` and write the finding into the slot, not a guess. Regenerate with `pnpm plugins` so `packages/codex-plugin/skills/**` follows, and extend `test/integration/plugin.test.ts` so the Codex decide and loop skills must name the tool. Out of scope: `approve` still elicits via askYes — that is node approve-asks-once-drop-the-leftover-asky-9818.

brief.approach:
Three files change by hand; the rest is generated.

1. `plugins/hosts/codex.json`, slot `ask`. Name the tool: "Ask with `request_user_input`, this host's own question tool — the one question, the option labels only". In the same sentence say when it is not there: Codex offers `request_user_input` per turn (its own instructions say to use it only when it is listed in the turn's tools; it is there in the interactive Default and Plan modes, never under `codex exec`). When it is not listed, ask in the conversation exactly as `plugins/hosts/opencode.json` does — the options in full, the reason for each, what each costs later — and wait for a reply that names one option. Keep the rest of the slot word for word with `claude.json` (pass `decide` exactly the pick; a yes and a no for a brief or a merge; `confirmed: true` only on an explicit yes; never answer on their behalf). One more clause, from the version check: Codex's own prompt tells the model never to use `request_user_input` for a permission request, so a brief or merge yes may fall to the conversation even in Default mode — that is fine, the rule is the same: a yes in the chat is a yes, silence is not.

2. `packages/codex-plugin/README.md`, under "What is different from Claude Code": one short paragraph, "Asking is per turn" — `request_user_input` is offered by mode, not always; when it is missing the skills ask in the chat. Verified against codex-cli 0.154.0.

3. `test/integration/plugin.test.ts`: extend the existing "every host's decision skill asks with the host's own question" test (line ~150) or add one beside it: for host `codex`, `decide`, `next`, `brief` and `loop` skills must contain `request_user_input` and the fallback phrase "when it is not listed" (or whatever the slot says — pick one exact phrase and assert it). Claude's must contain `AskUserQuestion` and not `request_user_input`; OpenCode's must contain neither.

4. `pnpm plugins` regenerates `packages/codex-plugin/skills/**`. Commit the generated files with the source.

Out of scope: `approve` still eliciting via askYes (node approve-asks-once-drop-the-leftover-asky-9818). Do not touch `plugins/skills/*/SKILL.md` — the slot is enough.

acceptance.proves: The slot names the tool and every generated Codex skill that asks carries the name
No other host's skills picked up Codex's tool name
The generated skills are in step with the source; nothing was hand-edited
The new Codex assertion passes and every existing skill test still holds
Lint, types and the rest of the repo's gate are green
